With the second-most runways in the United States, Dallas/Fort Worth is another of the nation's most prominent global gateways. The facility is not just a major hub for American Airlines and the oneworld alliance as a whole but is also the location of the legacy carrier's corporate headquarters.

An aerial view of Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. 

Photo: Todd MacDonald |  Wikimedia Commons [...] Denver International Airport, one of America's largest and hub for US-based legacy carrier United Airlines, primarily serves Colorado's Front Range Urban Corridor. The facility, which opened in 1995, replaced the earlier Stapleton Airport. It has been surrounded by mystery and conspiracy since its opening and offers some of the longest runways in the United States.

An aerial view of Denver International Airport. 

Photo: Murphpics | Wikimedia Commons [...] ### Summary

 Chicago O'Hare International Airport has the most runways of any civilian airport in the world, with 8 runways.
 Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport is the second-largest global hub in the US by passenger traffic, operating 7 runways.
 Denver International Airport has some of the longest runways in the US, with 6 total, and is known for its unique and mysterious history.

results.title: How long is an airport’s runway?
results.content: Between these two runway extremes sits a “typical” commercial airline runway length: roughly between 8,000 feet (2,438 meters) and 13,000 feet (3,962 meters). Although most airline passengers don’t give much thought to runway length, I sometimes hear the stray passenger remark during takeoff or landing, “I hope this runway is long enough.” [...] Many factors determine runway length including elevation above sea level. [...] Airport runway length is contingent on a number of factors, including aircraft type. The larger the aircraft, the longer the runway required. This makes sense when you consider that a typical commercial jetliner needs to reach 150 to 180 mph (240 to 285 km/h) to take off, and the larger the aircraft, the longer it takes to reach these speeds.
